correctness.rationale: Rotational invariance diagonalizes T_u on each homogeneous degree-n block with dimension binom(n+d-1,d-1). Beta integration yields lambda_n=Gamma(beta+is)/Gamma(beta)*Gamma(n+d+beta)/Gamma(n+d+beta+is). Its gamma-product modulus gives centered block eigenvalues r_n=c(product_(k>=0)(1+s²/(n+d+beta+k)²)-1)>0, decreasing to zero. Asymptotic log-product s²/n+O(n^-2) gives r_n=c s²/n+O(n^-2). The multiplicities sum to binom(n+d,d), proving s_j~c s²/(d!)^(1/d)*j^-1/d, S_p exactly p>d, and log endpoint (c s²)^d/d!. Q_s essential limit c-1 and unique centering 1-c follow. Gamma characteristic-function argument proves 0<c<1 for s!=0. Independent mpmath checks tested the first-order asymptotic in dimensions 1,3,4; these do not prove the infinite limit.

value.rationale: For a natural bounded but boundary-oscillating unimodular symbol, the raw semicommutator is noncompact while its unique scalar renormalization has a precise weak-S_d endpoint. The exact gamma coefficient and dimension threshold are useful invariants for rough-symbol Bergman operator ideals; this does not claim a general arbitrary-symbol theorem.
